title: The periodic table and periodic trends
note: Across a period, nuclear charge rises faster than shielding, so effective nuclear charge grows: atoms shrink, ionization energy rises, and electronegativity rises. Down a group, each new shell puts valence electrons farther out: atoms grow and hold their electrons less tightly. Known exceptions in ionization energy (Be > B, N > O) come from subshell structure.

read.title: Why the table has trends
text: The periodic table puts elements with similar valence electron configurations in the same column, so their chemistry repeats. Lithium, sodium, and potassium all have one s electron beyond a noble-gas core, and all are soft, reactive metals that form 1+ ions.

Trends in size and energy follow from one idea: how strongly the nucleus pulls on the outer electrons. Moving left to right across a period, each element adds a proton to the nucleus and an electron to the same shell. Electrons in the same shell shield each other poorly, so the effective nuclear charge felt by the outer electrons rises. The atoms shrink, it takes more energy to remove an electron, and electronegativity climbs. Moving down a group, a new shell is added each time. The outer electrons sit farther from the nucleus behind more inner electrons, so atoms get larger and lose electrons more easily.

Ions follow the same logic. A cation is smaller than its parent atom, and an anion is larger. For ions with the same number of electrons, the one with the most protons is the smallest. There are small exceptions to the ionization energy trend: boron is lower than beryllium, and oxygen is lower than nitrogen, because of how electrons sit in s and p subshells.

q.q: What causes atoms to shrink from left to right across a period?
o: Adding a new electron shell at each step
Rising effective nuclear charge on the outer electrons
Loss of protons from the nucleus

q.q: Why do lithium, sodium, and potassium behave alike?
o: They have the same atomic mass
They have the same number of shells
They share a similar valence electron configuration

q.q: Among ions with the same number of electrons, which is smallest?
o: The one with the most protons
The one with the fewest protons
The one with the most neutrons
